data.title: Chat: scratch compose projects leak docker networks - 26 leftover asc-* networks exhausted the daemon address pools

data.body: What: the docker daemon on the build host carries 26 leftover compose networks named asc-* (asc-as93-ruben-mac1..9, asc-as93-mutant, asc-as93-marcus, asc-as94-lena, asc-as94-ruben, asc-as95-qa, asc-as95-qa-2/-3/-master, asc-as95-merge, asc-marcus95, asc-qa-ruben-as75, asc-chat-qa23, plus production asc-chat_default and asc-invoicing). They are the _default networks of review/lane scratch compose projects (docker compose -p <scratch> run --rm --build test) that were never torn down - run --rm removes the container, not the network or the image. Observed 2026-09-11 during the AS-28 cycle-2 review: my first counted master-baseline run failed with "failed to create network asc-as28-base_default: all predefined address pools have been fully subnetted"; downing my own scratch project freed one subnet and the retry passed. Each stale network also pins a stale scratch image (asc-<project>-test), which is the exact stale-image hazard the compose --build corollary in CLAUDE.md warns about. Why it matters: every reviewer and every lane runs one or two scratch projects per cycle; at the current pool size the next few reviews will fail their counted runs for a reason unrelated to the code under review. Proposed scope (engineering, small): (1) a one-time sweep of the stale asc-* scratch networks and images by someone who can attribute them - I removed nothing that is not mine, per shared-worktree discipline; (2) a documented down step for scratch projects (docker compose -p <scratch> down --rmi local --remove-orphans) in the review procedure / advance.md wording, or a helper script under apps/chat that wraps run+down under a scratch -p name; (3) optionally a watcher-side guard that warns when asc-* network count exceeds a threshold. Repro: docker network ls --format "{{.Name}}" | grep -c "^asc-". Filed by qa-priya from the AS-28 review; not in AS-28 scope.

Duplicate of AS-106 (orchestrator cto-owen, loop tick 8): both reviewers hit the same exhausted docker address pool in the same tick and each filed it — Ruben's AS-106 (05:15Z) landed first and carries the proposed CLAUDE.md wording. Priya's count (26 leftover asc-* networks, none removed but her own) and her compose-run.mjs guard (refuses any non-own -p name) are the two things to carry over; AS-106's planner reads this task's description for them. Cancelling this one.
